original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-2-product-categories-fibred-setoids}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
The 2-category of categories fibred in setoids over $\mathcal{C}$
has 2-fibre products. More precisely, the 2-fibre product described in
Lemma \ref{lemma-2-product-categories-over-C} returns a category fibred in
setoids if one starts out with such.
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal S$ and $G:\mathcal Y\to\mathcal S$ be morphisms of categories fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$. Their $2$-fibre product exists in the $2$-category of categories fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$. Explicitly, its objects are quadruples $(U,x,y,\alpha)$ with $U\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$, $x\in\mathcal X_U$, $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, and $\alpha:F(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(y)$ in $\mathcal S_U$. Its morphisms are pairs $(a,b)$ over the same base arrow $U\to U'$ satisfying $G(b)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ F(a)$. This again defines a category fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$ and, with its projections, has the stated universal property.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, and let $\mathcal X\to\mathcal S\leftarrow\mathcal Y$ be a span of categories fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$.
conclusions: Their $2$-fibre product exists in the $2$-category of categories fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$. Explicitly, its objects are quadruples $(U,x,y,\alpha)$ with $U\in\Ob(\mathcal C)$, $x\in\mathcal X_U$, $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, and $\alpha:F(x)\xrightarrow{\sim}G(y)$ in $\mathcal S_U$. Its morphisms are pairs $(a,b)$ over the same base arrow $U\to U'$ satisfying $G(b)\circ\alpha=\alpha'\circ F(a)$. This again defines a category fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$ and, with its projections, has the stated universal property.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-setoid-fibres}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category. Let $\mathcal{S}$ be a category
over $\mathcal{C}$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $\mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{S}'$ is an equivalence
over $\mathcal{C}$ with $\mathcal{S}'$ fibred in sets over $\mathcal{C}$,
then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{S}$ is fibred in setoids over $\mathcal{C}$, and
\item for each $U \in \Ob(\mathcal{C})$ the map
$\Ob(\mathcal{S}_U) \to \Ob(\mathcal{S}'_U)$
identifies the target as the set of isomorphism classes of the source.
\end{enumerate}
\item If $p : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{C}$ is a category fibred in setoids,
then there exists a category fibred in sets
$p' : \mathcal{S}' \to \mathcal{C}$ and an equivalence
$\text{can} : \mathcal{S} \to \mathcal{S}'$ over $\mathcal{C}$.
\end{enumerate}

hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category, and define $F(\mathcal S)_U$ as the discrete category of isomorphism classes of objects in $\mathcal S_U$ for $\mathcal S$ fibred in setoids.
conclusions:
This functor is an equivalence in the following sense:
\begin{enumerate}
\item for any two 1-morphisms $f, g : \mathcal{S}_1 \to \mathcal{S}_2$
with $F(f) = F(g)$ there exists a unique 2-isomorphism $f \to g$,
\item for any morphism $h : F(\mathcal{S}_1) \to F(\mathcal{S}_2)$
there exists a 1-morphism $f : \mathcal{S}_1 \to \mathcal{S}_2$
with $F(f) = h$, and
\item any category fibred in sets $\mathcal{S}$ is equal to $F(\mathcal{S})$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, defining $F_i \in \textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})$ by the
rule $F_i(U) = \Ob(\mathcal{S}_{i, U})/\cong$, we have
$$
\Mor_{\textit{Cat}/\mathcal{C}}(\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2)
\Big/
2\text{-isomorphism}
=
\Mor_{\textit{PSh}(\mathcal{C})}(F_1, F_2)
$$
More precisely, given any map $\phi : F_1 \to F_2$ there exists a
$1$-morphism $f : \mathcal{S}_1 \to \mathcal{S}_2$ which induces
$\phi$ on isomorphism classes of objects and
which is unique up to unique $2$-isomorphism.

original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-category-fibred-setoids-presheaves-products}
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
The construction of
Lemma \ref{lemma-2-category-fibred-setoids}
which associates to a category fibred in setoids a presheaf is
compatible with products, in the sense that the presheaf associated
to a $2$-fibre product $\mathcal{X} \times_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z}$
is the fibre product of the presheaves associated to
$\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z}$.
statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a category.
For each category $\mathcal T$ fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$, define the presheaf $P_{\mathcal T}(U)=\Ob(\mathcal T_U)/\cong$. This assignment is
compatible with products, in the sense that the presheaf associated
to a $2$-fibre product $\mathcal{X} \times_\mathcal{Y} \mathcal{Z}$
is the fibre product of the presheaves associated to
$\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z}$.
hypotheses: Let $\mathcal C$ be a category and $\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y\leftarrow\mathcal Z$ a span of categories fibred in setoids over $\mathcal C$. Define $P_\mathcal T(U)=\Ob(\mathcal T_U)/\cong$.
conclusions: $P_{\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal Z}\cong P_{\mathcal X}\times_{P_{\mathcal Y}}P_{\mathcal Z}$ as presheaves on $\mathcal C$.
